title: Classes & Object-Oriented Blueprint
description: Classes define object blueprints encapsulating state attributes and behavior methods with inheritance and encapsulation.

quiz.question: What are the four core pillars of Object-Oriented Programming (OOP)?
options: Compilation, Linking, Execution, and Garbage Collection.
quiz.explanation: The 4 fundamental pillars of OOP are Encapsulation (bundling state/methods), Abstraction (hiding implementation details), Inheritance (reusing parent class code), and Polymorphism (overriding interface behavior).

interviewQuestions.q: 01. What is the role of `self` in Python class methods?
interviewQuestions.a: `self` is an explicit reference to the current instance object invoking the method. It binds instance attributes (`self.name = name`) to the specific Heap object.

interviewQuestions.q: 02. What is the difference between `__init__()` vs `__new__()` in Python?
interviewQuestions.a: `__new__()` is the actual constructor that instantiates and returns a new object instance in memory. `__init__()` is the initializer that sets up instance attributes.

interviewQuestions.q: 03. What is the difference between Class Variables vs Instance Variables?
interviewQuestions.a: Class variables are declared directly inside the class body and shared across ALL instances. Instance variables are defined inside `__init__()` using `self` and exist independently per instance.

interviewQuestions.q: 04. What is Encapsulation and how are private attributes (`__private`) represented in Python?
interviewQuestions.a: Encapsulation restricts direct access to internal object state. Double underscores (`__private`) trigger Name Mangling (`_ClassName__private`) to prevent accidental subclass overrides.

interviewQuestions.q: 05. What is Method Overriding vs Method Overloading?
interviewQuestions.a: Method Overriding replaces a parent class method in a subclass. Method Overloading defines multiple methods with the same name but different parameter signatures (supported natively in Java/C++, simulated via default args in Python).

interviewQuestions.q: 06. How does Multiple Inheritance work and what is Method Resolution Order (MRO)?
interviewQuestions.a: Python allows a class to inherit from multiple parent classes. The C3 Linearization algorithm determines the exact search order (MRO) accessed via `ClassName.mro()` or `__mro__`.

interviewQuestions.q: 07. What is `super()` and why should it be used in constructor inheritance?
interviewQuestions.a: `super().__init__()` delegates constructor initialization to parent classes following the MRO chain without hardcoding parent class names.

interviewQuestions.q: 08. What are Python Dunder (Magic) Methods (`__str__`, `__repr__`, `__len__`, `__eq__`)?
interviewQuestions.a: Special double-underscore methods that hook custom class objects into Python operators and built-in functions (e.g. `__str__` for `print()`, `__eq__` for `==`).

interviewQuestions.q: 09. What is `@classmethod` vs `@staticmethod` in Python?
interviewQuestions.a: `@classmethod` takes `cls` as first argument and can access class state (useful for factory constructors). `@staticmethod` takes no implicit first argument and acts as a plain function scoped inside the class namespace.

interviewQuestions.q: 10. What is `@property` decorator (Getters & Setters) in Python?
interviewQuestions.a: `@property` turns a method into a read-only attribute getter. `@var.setter` defines setter validation logic, enforcing encapsulation cleanly without changing caller syntax (`obj.var = val`).

interviewQuestions.q: 11. What is Abstract Base Class (ABC) in Python?
interviewQuestions.a: Using `from abc import ABC, abstractmethod`, an Abstract Base Class defines mandatory interface methods that subclasses MUST implement, preventing direct instantiation of incomplete base classes.

interviewQuestions.q: 12. What are Python `__slots__` and how do they optimize RAM memory?
interviewQuestions.a: Defining `__slots__ = ('name', 'age')` replaces the dynamic instance dictionary `__dict__` with a fixed-size C array, saving up to 40-50% RAM memory per object instance.

interviewQuestions.q: 13. What is Polymorphism and Duck Typing in Python?
interviewQuestions.a: Polymorphism lets different objects respond to identical method calls. Python uses Duck Typing: 'If it walks like a duck and quacks like a duck, it's a duck' (focuses on object capability rather than explicit class type).

interviewQuestions.q: 14. What is Virtual Method Table (VTable) in C++ / Java OOP?
interviewQuestions.a: A lookup table of function pointers used by object runtimes to dynamically dispatch overridden virtual methods at runtime.

interviewQuestions.q: 15. What is Composition vs Inheritance ('Has-a' vs 'Is-a')?
interviewQuestions.a: Inheritance ('Is-a') creates tight coupling between classes. Composition ('Has-a') combines decoupled object instances as fields, providing higher flexibility and easier maintenance.

interviewQuestions.q: 16. What is the SOLID Principles of Object-Oriented Design?
interviewQuestions.a: Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, and Dependency Inversion principles guiding maintainable software architecture.

interviewQuestions.q: 17. How does Python Garbage Collection (Reference Counting + Cyclic GC) manage object destruction?
interviewQuestions.a: Python tracks reference counts per object. When reference count drops to 0, memory is immediately freed. A cyclic garbage collector periodically detects circular reference deadlocks.

interviewQuestions.q: 18. What is `__del__()` destructor in Python and why is it unreliable?
interviewQuestions.a: `__del__()` is called when an object is about to be garbage collected, but execution timing is not guaranteed. Use context managers (`with` statement) for reliable resource cleanup instead.

interviewQuestions.q: 19. What is a Dataclass (`@dataclass`) in Python 3.7+?
interviewQuestions.a: `@dataclass` automatically generates `__init__()`, `__repr__()`, and `__eq__()` methods for classes primarily holding data fields.

interviewQuestions.q: 20. What are production best practices for Object-Oriented Design?
interviewQuestions.a: Favor composition over inheritance, keep class responsibilities tightly focused, enforce private attributes with `@property`, and leverage dataclasses for clean data transfer objects.
